content:
tess-customer: Hi team — noticed weird behavior on streaming after a flaky mobile connection. When the client reconnects we sometimes get duplicated partial chunks and truncated final outputs. Also saw an unexpected billing spike this morning for token usage. Anyone else seeing this?

maria: sorry about that, can you share the session id + approximate timestamps? and a short repro if possible? :sorry: we’ll escalate.

tess-customer: session: sess_9b2f4, first seen ~1852001400 UTC. Repro is easy on our side: toggle airplane mode for ~2–3s during a long stream then reconnect. Client does automatic resume with the resume_token returned earlier. Example client code below (very small):

```js
// simplified pseudocode
const es = new EventSource(url + '?resume_token=' + token);
es.onmessage = (e) => { renderChunk(e.data); };
// on disconnect we re-open and pass same resume_token
```

When reconnect happens we sometimes get the last ~2 chunks repeated interleaved with new ones, and final message truncated. Billing shows ~2x tokens for that session.

maria: thanks, that's helpful. Do you send any idempotency key / request-id in the headers?

tess-customer: we set `x-client-request-id` for the original request but not for resumptions — resume is supposed to be a follow-on on the same session.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-129 — streaming-resume-duplication (priority P2)

jordan: @maria @sam tagging in eng-platform. From past bugs, duplication often happens when the client resumes and the server emits overlapping prefix tokens while also replaying cached tail chunks. Can you dump the server-side stream events for the session? need `seq` numbers and resume token contents.

maria: I have a partial log from the customer timeframe, sanitized:

```
[1852001398] sess sess_9b2f4 start stream seq=1
[1852001405] emit chunk seq=1 tokens=120 event_id=ev-A
[1852001410] emit chunk seq=2 tokens=64 event_id=ev-B
[1852001411] client disconnected (timeout)
[1852001413] received resume with token resume_seq=2 client_offset=186
[1852001414] replay cached chunk seq=2 tokens=64 event_id=ev-B
[1852001415] emit new chunk seq=3 tokens=90 event_id=ev-C
[1852001420] emit final chunk seq=4 tokens=50 event_id=ev-D
```

jordan: hmm logs show server replayed seq=2 after resume, but client also got cached prefix that included a partial of seq=2 before reconnect — that could cause duplicated tokens on the client and double-billing if both replay and new emission are counted. Billing counts are per-emitted-token currently.

lee: from an inference runtime perspective, duplication can come from two paths: 1) client retrieved a partial stream and locally buffered output (so it shows repeated text when server replays), 2) server-side double-emit due to race while resuming KV cache pointers. The event_id in logs is useful — if we had unique event_ids on SSE lines, we could dedupe at billing and client can skip already-seen ids.

sam: short-term: we can do server-side dedupe on event_id within a sliding window per-session before counting billing events. Medium-term: tighten resume semantics so resume_token includes last_ack_seq and server waits to confirm client ack before replaying older seqs.

maria: customer reporting token billing doubled for that session. any way to retroactively adjust billing while we investigate?

sam: ops can issue a one-off credit if we confirm duplication pattern. I'll open billing case and hold charges pending logs.

jordan: two engineering actions I propose: (A) enforce that resume flow includes `last_ack_seq` — if client doesn't provide it server should not replay chunks older than that; (B) add server dedupe by `event_id` + session dedupe window.

lee: additional idea: embed a `token_offset` in every SSE message and a consistent per-token `token_seq` id. Client can send its last-seen `token_seq` on resume and we can resume from next unique token. This avoids ambiguity with chunk boundaries.

maria: tess — can you check if your client stores the last event_id / token_offset locally when network drops?

tess-customer: we have lastEventId saved but our SDK only rewrites resume_token; we don't include lastEventId in the resume call currently. probably that’s the missing piece.

jordan: good catch. That explains mismatch: client believes it has seen up to some byte-offset, but server replay uses resume token that is coarser. Result: overlap.

maria: for immediate mitigation — tess, can you test a quick client patch that sends `last_event_id` in the resume query param and confirm? If that suppresses duplicates we can ship guidance and a short-term SDK patch.

tess-customer: can try in the morning and report back. thanks.

sam: infra hotfix plan (short): when resume is received, compute `replay_start_seq = max(resume_seq, last_ack_seq+1)` where `last_ack_seq` is from client if present. If client not present, use resume_seq but mark tokens in overlap window as non-billable once deduped. Rolling deploy low-risk change.

jordan: also adding unit tests to cover interleaved replay + new emission race. I've opened PR #1428 to add both dedupe and a strict resume handshake: server replies with `resume_ack:{confirmed_seq: N}` before replaying. Client should wait for ack.

lee: note: this will also require updates to our runtime KV pointers so we don't reset to an older KV state if new tokens were generated in the race window. I'll coordinate with eng-runtime.

maria: immediate customer communication: I drafted a short note: "we're investigating duplicated partial outputs during mobile reconnects. workaround: update SDK to include last event id in resume requests; we're testing a server-side fix and will follow up with credits for impacted sessions." Approve? :thumbsup:

jordan: approve, send. Also log action items: 1) Customer patch guidance + example curl SDK snippet; 2) server hotfix deploy (dedupe + resume_ack); 3) billing review and credits; 4) regression tests.

maria: recording action items and owners. I'll circle back after customer confirms quick patch.

--- example resume curl snippet sent to customer ---

curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?session_id=sess_9b2f4&resume_token=rt_abc&last_event_id=ev-B"

--- end snippet ---

incident-bot: INC-2026-129 updated: engineering working on hotfix.

maria: thanks everyone. tess — please ping here after you test the `last_event_id` resume. we'll coordinate credits if duplication reproduced. :pray:

tess-customer: will do, thanks all.
